one_line_idea: SAM's output granularity (part vs whole) is a near-deterministic function of click position relative to the object's medial axis, not a reflection of genuine ambiguity resolution.
core_hypothesis: The scale of the mask SAM returns for a single point is predictable from purely geometric prompt features (distance to nearest boundary, distance to medial axis) independent of image semantics.

one_line_idea: Box-prompt slack acts as an undocumented continuous scale prompt: SAM reads how loose a box is as a tolerance signal, so mask area inflates predictably with box dilation even when the object is unambiguous.
core_hypothesis: SAM's decoder uses box corner embeddings as a soft scale prior, so mask area is a smooth increasing function of box slack rather than a step function that saturates once the object is enclosed.

one_line_idea: Although SAM encodes point sets symmetrically, PEFT-finetuned interactive variants develop click-order sensitivity, breaking the set-invariance contract users rely on.
core_hypothesis: Fine-tuning with iterative click simulation induces dependence on click order via the previous-mask input channel, so permuting the same click set changes final masks substantially more in adapted models than in frozen SAM.

one_line_idea: Negative clicks are strictly weaker than positive clicks in SAM: removing an over-segmented region takes systematically more clicks than adding an equivalent under-segmented region, revealing an asymmetric prompt algebra.
core_hypothesis: SAM's training distribution contained far fewer informative negative clicks, so the decoder's subtraction capacity is lower than its addition capacity for regions of matched area and boundary complexity.

one_line_idea: Prompt-jitter robustness is a leading indicator of domain-shift robustness: PEFT-adapted SAMs lose click-jitter stability before their centroid-click accuracy drops, giving a label-free early-warning metric for over-adaptation.
core_hypothesis: Over-adaptation first manifests as a shrinking basin of prompt attraction (masks change under small click jitter) while best-prompt accuracy is still intact, because the model narrows its prompt-conditioned decision boundaries before moving them.

one_line_idea: Most objects contain interior adversarial click points where frozen SAM returns near-zero-IoU masks, and these failure points cluster along internal texture boundaries rather than being random.
core_hypothesis: The click-to-mask map has a structured failure set: interior points near strong internal gradients (logos, seams, shadows) reliably produce part-like or degenerate masks, and this set is stable across model seeds and image augmentations.

one_line_idea: Masks produced by SAM's automatic everything mode are frequently not reproducible by any single click, meaning automatic and interactive SAM are effectively two different segmenters sharing weights.
core_hypothesis: A non-trivial fraction of everything-mode masks cannot be recovered above a high-IoU threshold by any single point prompt in the image, because they arise from NMS interactions between multiple prompt seeds.

one_line_idea: When box and point prompts conflict, SAM resolves the conflict by a fixed learned hierarchy rather than evidence weighting, and PEFT silently reorders that hierarchy, changing pipeline behavior without any accuracy metric noticing.
core_hypothesis: Frozen SAM has a consistent dominance ordering (e.g., box constrains, point selects within) under conflicting prompts, and LoRA adaptation on a domain where one prompt type dominated training data measurably shifts this ordering.

one_line_idea: Because SAM rescales every image to a fixed input resolution, the same physical click has resolution-dependent semantics: click informativeness and effective precision degrade lawfully with source image size, an unmodeled shift for high-resolution domains.
core_hypothesis: There exists a lawful relationship between source resolution and both minimum-selectable-object-size and click-precision requirements, fully explained by the fixed internal resolution, and tiling strategies change the prompt semantics rather than merely adding compute.

one_line_idea: LoRA adaptation of SAM to shifted domains mostly learns low-order intensity and color recalibration, not new shape priors: matched-histogram preprocessing recovers most of the LoRA gain without any weight updates.
core_hypothesis: For modality-style shifts (grayscale, stain variation, sensor gamma), the function computed by encoder LoRA is well-approximated by a per-channel monotone intensity transform of the input, so its benefit largely disappears once inputs are histogram-matched to the pretraining distribution.

one_line_idea: Rank-1 LoRA is sufficient for modality-level adaptation of SAM, and everything above rank 1 fits annotation style rather than domain content, measurable by cross-annotator generalization.
core_hypothesis: The domain-content component of adaptation lives in a one-dimensional weight-update subspace, while higher-rank components encode annotation-protocol idiosyncrasies, so higher rank helps same-annotator test sets but hurts or does not help different-annotator test sets of the same domain.

one_line_idea: Where LoRA is placed in SAM changes what is learned, not just how much: attention-projection LoRA learns spatial grouping changes while MLP LoRA learns appearance re-mapping, yielding qualitatively different error profiles at equal parameter count.
core_hypothesis: Attention-path adapters mainly change which pixels group together (affecting under- and over-merging errors) while MLP-path adapters mainly change appearance interpretation (affecting missed-object and texture-confusion errors), and this dissociation is visible in error-type-decomposed metrics.

one_line_idea: Decoder-only PEFT can match encoder PEFT for many domain shifts because the gap manifests as prompt-token-to-feature misalignment rather than feature deficiency, contradicting the default that the encoder must adapt.
core_hypothesis: Frozen SAM encoder features remain linearly sufficient to separate object from background in many shifted domains, and failures arise because the decoder's cross-attention queries no longer align with feature statistics; hence adapting only the two-layer decoder (a tiny parameter set) recovers most of the achievable gain.

one_line_idea: Task-specific PEFT silently destroys SAM's ambiguity machinery: after adaptation, the three multimask outputs collapse toward one mask, removing a capability no downstream metric tracks.
core_hypothesis: Fine-tuning on datasets with unique ground-truth masks provides gradient pressure that collapses the output-token diversity, so inter-mask IoU among the three outputs rises toward 1.0 as adaptation proceeds, at a rate set by dataset ambiguity level.

one_line_idea: Adapter-tuned SAM exhibits within-image interference: adaptation for target structures measurably degrades masks for untouched object categories present in the same images, a ripple effect invisible to target-only evaluation.
core_hypothesis: Because encoder adapters alter the shared feature field of the whole image, improving target-structure segmentation redistributes feature geometry and degrades non-target masks in the same scenes more than on unrelated scenes, i.e., interference is spatially and contextually coupled.

one_line_idea: Bias-only tuning (BitFit-style) of SAM matches LoRA on texture- and intensity-shifted domains, implying that most claimed domain adaptation for segmentation is feature re-centering, not feature re-learning.
core_hypothesis: Distribution shift in many target domains moves feature means more than feature directions, so additive per-channel corrections (biases, LayerNorm parameters) capture most recoverable gain, with LoRA's advantage confined to shifts that rotate feature geometry.

one_line_idea: Under sequential PEFT, promptability forgets faster than features: SAM adapted to domain B after domain A retains transferable features (linear probes stay strong) while interactive behavior on domain A collapses, locating forgetting in the prompt pathway.
core_hypothesis: Feature geometry is anchored by massive pretraining and moves slowly under sequential low-rank updates, whereas the prompt-conditioned readout is low-dimensional and brittle, so forgetting measured via prompts vastly overstates forgetting measured via probes.

one_line_idea: Weight-space merging of independently trained domain LoRAs works unusually well for SAM (compared to classification adapters) because prompt conditioning absorbs cross-domain conflicts, making the merged model a testbed for when adapter arithmetic succeeds.
core_hypothesis: Conflicts between domain adapters mostly concern which structure to segment, a decision the prompt already resolves at inference; therefore merged LoRAs retain most per-domain performance in promptable mode while the same merge fails in prompt-free (semantic head) mode, isolating prompting as the conflict absorber.

one_line_idea: Visual prompt-token tuning (VPT-style) preserves SAM's everything-mode and zero-shot behavior far better than LoRA at equal target-domain accuracy, because appended tokens cannot rewrite spatial feature geometry.
core_hypothesis: There is a method-class law: input-space and token-space adaptation (learned prompts, prefix tokens) trade a small target-accuracy ceiling for large capability retention, while weight-space adaptation (LoRA, adapters) does the reverse, and the trade-off is governed by whether the method can alter token-mixing pathways.

one_line_idea: SAM's predicted-IoU head is a mask-style critic, not an accuracy estimator: under domain shift its score tracks smoothness and compactness of the mask more than true IoU, which breaks every pipeline that uses the score for filtering.
core_hypothesis: The IoU head learned features of masks that correlated with quality in-distribution (compactness, boundary smoothness, closed topology) and regresses onto those features; under shift the correlation with true IoU collapses while correlation with style features persists.

one_line_idea: During PEFT, calibration of the IoU head collapses before mask quality does, so score-vs-truth divergence on a small probe set is an early-warning signal for harmful over-adaptation.
core_hypothesis: The IoU head sits downstream of adapted features but is rarely included in PEFT parameter sets, so feature drift first appears as miscalibration of the frozen head, measurable epochs before held-out mask accuracy declines.

one_line_idea: SAM's own score distribution is a free domain-shift detector: the shape of predicted-IoU histograms over grid prompts detects out-of-distribution imagery as well as dedicated feature-space OOD methods, at zero additional model cost.
core_hypothesis: Competence-relevant shift compresses and shifts the grid-prompt score distribution in characteristic ways (mass moving off the high-score mode), so simple statistics of that distribution predict per-image segmentation quality drop better than generic feature-distance OOD scores.

one_line_idea: SAM's ambiguity bottleneck is ranking, not generation: the correct mask is frequently among the three outputs but not top-ranked, so fixing selection (a tiny head) would harvest most of the oracle-vs-deployed gap.
core_hypothesis: Under domain shift, mask-generation capability degrades slower than ranking capability, so the fraction of cases where the oracle mask exists but is misranked grows with shift, and retraining only the selection mechanism on few labels recovers most of the oracle gap.

one_line_idea: Disagreement between SAM's stability score and its predicted IoU score is a label-error detector: pixels-cheap, model-free-of-extra-training, and usable to audit ground truth in segmentation datasets.
core_hypothesis: When SAM is prompted with ground-truth-derived prompts, cases where stability score is high but agreement with ground truth is low are enriched for annotation errors rather than model errors, because the two scores capture independent evidence about boundary support.

one_line_idea: SAM's three multimask outputs are not diverse hypotheses but a hard-coded scale quantization (part, object, group), which predicts a specific failure family on structures without hierarchical scale organization.
core_hypothesis: The three output tokens specialize to nested scale levels during training, so for prompts whose plausible masks are non-nested alternatives at similar scale, SAM returns three near-nested masks and misses at least one valid alternative entirely.

one_line_idea: Variance across SAM's internal token-to-image attention maps localizes boundary errors: an unused, training-free per-pixel uncertainty map already exists inside the decoder.
core_hypothesis: Disagreement among cross-attention patterns of the output token across decoder layers and heads concentrates precisely where the produced boundary is wrong, because attention disagreement reflects unresolved evidence integration.

one_line_idea: SAM encoder features are excellent boundary features but poor semantic features, and the two qualities anti-correlate across layers, refuting the assumption that a segmentation foundation model is a general visual foundation model.
core_hypothesis: Class-agnostic mask supervision optimized the encoder for where-things-end rather than what-things-are, so linear probes show SAM below weaker self-supervised baselines on semantic tasks while dominating on boundary and grouping tasks, with the gap widening in later layers.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Contrarian against 'segmentation foundation model = general visual foundation model'; boundary/semantic anti-correlation across layers is a checkable dissociation.

one_line_idea: SAM inherits a persistent MAE fingerprint: its failure modes align with reconstruction-pretraining biases (low-level statistics, local completion) more than with its segmentation training, measurable by comparing against a counterfactual contrastive-initialized SAM.
core_hypothesis: A substantial share of SAM's characteristic errors (texture leakage, completion of occluded regions, insensitivity to global semantics) is inherited from generative-reconstruction pretraining and would differ qualitatively had the encoder been initialized contrastively, even with identical segmentation training.

one_line_idea: The layer-wise need for adaptation in SAM is U-shaped: earliest and final encoder layers require updates while the middle two-thirds are domain-universal, contradicting both adapt-everything and adapt-last-layers defaults.
core_hypothesis: Early layers encode sensor and texture statistics (shift-sensitive), late layers interface with the decoder's expectations (shift-sensitive), and middle layers compute generic grouping (shift-tolerant), so per-layer adaptation gain follows a U-shape across depths and across domains.

one_line_idea: SAM's windowed-attention design leaves a grid fingerprint: under domain shift, segmentation errors cluster along the window boundaries of the ViT, an architecture-induced spatial artifact nobody audits for.
core_hypothesis: Because most encoder layers use windowed attention with only sparse global layers, cross-window integration is weaker, and under shift (where features are noisier) mask boundary errors and mask fragmentation align with the internal window lattice at rates far above chance.

one_line_idea: Despite being trained to find boundaries, SAM remains texture-biased in the cue-conflict sense: when shape and texture disagree, its groupings follow texture, showing that segmentation training does not confer shape bias.
core_hypothesis: Class-agnostic mask training rewards locally-consistent-region detection, which texture statistics support more cheaply than global shape, so SAM's decisions in cue-conflict stimuli (shape of A, texture of B) side with texture at rates comparable to ImageNet-trained ViTs.

one_line_idea: Token-norm inflation under domain shift maps where adaptation is needed: per-layer feature-norm statistics on unlabeled target images predict the optimal LoRA placement, enabling data-driven adapter allocation without any labels.
core_hypothesis: Layers whose token-norm and activation-statistics deviate most from natural-image reference statistics under target-domain inputs are the layers where LoRA insertion yields the largest gain, because statistical deviation marks broken computations.

one_line_idea: Aspect-ratio distortion from SAM's square-padded resizing is a first-order hidden failure source for thin elongated structures, rivaling texture shift in damage but fixable by inference-time letterboxing choices alone.
core_hypothesis: Performance loss on thin-structure domains decomposes into an appearance component and a preprocessing-geometry component, with the geometry component dominating when structures are near the internal resolution limit; changing only padding, tiling, and positional-embedding handling recovers it.

one_line_idea: SAM is unusually sensitive to JPEG and resampling artifacts because SA-1B consisted of high-quality licensed photography, making compression level an unmodeled domain axis that hits SAM harder than supervised baselines.
core_hypothesis: The pretraining corpus's uniformly high image quality created a quality-blind spot: boundary-acuity features exploit high-frequency detail that compression destroys, so SAM's boundary quality degrades faster with compression strength than that of models trained on messy web data.

one_line_idea: SAM's encoder exhibits high-norm outlier tokens (register-like sinks), and their spatial positions correlate with mask leakage errors, linking a known ViT pathology to concrete segmentation failures for the first time.
core_hypothesis: SAM's encoder develops a small set of high-norm tokens at semantically vacant positions; because the decoder reads the spatial feature map directly, these positions carry corrupted local information and are enriched among pixels where masks leak or fragment.

one_line_idea: An adaptability meter for SAM: pre-adaptation representation-similarity between frozen SAM features and a tiny target-domain-supervised probe network predicts final PEFT gain, letting teams forecast adaptation ROI before spending compute.
core_hypothesis: The achievable PEFT gain is governed by how much target-relevant structure frozen features already contain but misalign, which is measurable as the gap between (a) similarity of frozen SAM features to features of a small net trained on 50 target images and (b) frozen SAM's zero-shot performance; large similarity with poor zero-shot predicts large PEFT gain.

one_line_idea: The two-layer mask decoder, not the encoder, is the binding constraint for dense thin structures: deepening only the decoder (keeping the encoder frozen) recovers vessel- and crack-like segmentation that encoder PEFT cannot, at a fraction of the parameters.
core_hypothesis: Segmenting elongated connected structures requires iterative evidence propagation proportional to structure length; two decoder layers implement a fixed small number of propagation steps, so failures scale with structure tortuosity and are relieved by decoder depth, not encoder adaptation.

one_line_idea: SAM's mask tokens are overloaded scale-generalists: forcing token specialization by object scale (a handful of scale-conditioned output tokens) tests whether token capacity, not feature quality, limits small-object segmentation.
core_hypothesis: A single output token's query vector cannot be simultaneously optimal for all scales, so the effective operating point is biased toward the training-mass scale; adding scale-dedicated tokens (trained briefly, all else frozen) disproportionately improves off-modal scales.

one_line_idea: SAM has a constant systematic boundary offset (not proportional jitter) traceable to its 4x upsampling path, which means a universal sub-pixel correction could improve every SAM output at zero model cost.
core_hypothesis: The learned upsampling path induces a content-independent boundary displacement field (systematic erosion or dilation of a fixed sub-pixel magnitude, possibly orientation-dependent), detectable by aggregating signed boundary errors over many objects and correctable by a fixed morphological adjustment.

one_line_idea: Promptable segmentation cannot express relationally-defined regions (the gap between two objects, the part of A occluded by B), a representational blind spot of prompt-as-locator interfaces that no amount of PEFT fixes.
core_hypothesis: SAM's decoder implements approximate appearance-similarity expansion around the prompt, so regions whose definition requires relations rather than appearance coherence (gaps, shadows-of, occluded-parts-of) sit outside the reachable output set regardless of prompt engineering, and PEFT shifts but does not remove the boundary.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Representational blind spot (relationally defined regions unreachable by prompt-as-locator) that no PEFT fixes; attacks the interface, not the weights.

one_line_idea: The hypernetwork MLP mapping mask tokens to dynamic convolution weights in SAM is effectively linear: distilling it to a linear map costs almost nothing, revealing that the decoder's expressive component is placed where expressivity is not used.
core_hypothesis: Across prompts and images, the token-to-filter MLP's input-output map is well-approximated by its best linear fit (high R-squared), and swapping in the linear fit changes masks negligibly; the decoder's nonlinear work is concentrated in attention, not filter generation.

one_line_idea: Prompt tokens dilute output tokens in decoder self-attention: SAM's accuracy degradation with many clicks is an attention-budget artifact with a predictable functional form, fixable by attention masking rather than retraining.
core_hypothesis: As prompt-token count grows, the output token's self-attention allocation to informative tokens shrinks roughly inversely, degrading integration; renormalizing or masking self-attention at inference restores monotonicity without weight changes.

one_line_idea: Encoder-side PEFT breaks an implicit encoder-decoder contract in SAM: feature drift makes the frozen decoder's cross-attention read features it was never calibrated for, and a contract-violation metric predicts when joint (vs encoder-only) tuning is required.
core_hypothesis: The frozen decoder tolerates feature drift up to a threshold measurable as divergence of decoder cross-attention statistics (entropy, focus location) from their pretraining regime; beyond it, encoder-only tuning saturates and joint tuning pulls ahead, with the threshold consistent across domains.

one_line_idea: SAM's decoder cannot represent holes below a scale threshold: mask topology is systematically simplified (genus reduced) as hole size shrinks, defining a topological failure family with a measurable critical scale.
core_hypothesis: The coarse internal grid plus smooth upsampling acts as a low-pass filter on the mask indicator function, so holes below a critical fraction of object scale are filled with probability approaching one, and the critical scale is predictable from the internal feature resolution and stable across content.

one_line_idea: SAM2's memory bank induces confirmation bias: early mask errors are written to memory and then re-read as evidence, making per-object error growth superlinear after occlusions in a way promptless re-initialization would avoid.
core_hypothesis: Because memory attention conditions current predictions on past predicted masks, an error written at time t raises the probability of the same error at t+1 beyond what frame difficulty explains, creating a self-reinforcing loop whose strength grows with the number of memory slots the error occupies.

one_line_idea: SAM2's object memory encodes appearance rather than identity: repeated similar objects (twins, uniform players, identical parts) cause identity swaps at rates predictable from appearance similarity alone, exposing the absence of spatiotemporal identity binding.
core_hypothesis: Swap probability at crossing or proximity events is a monotone function of feature-space similarity between target and distractor, approximately independent of motion-continuity cues that would trivially disambiguate for a tracker with a motion model, revealing that memory attention lacks positional-continuity binding.

one_line_idea: Video training regressed SAM2's single-image behavior in specific structure families relative to SAM1 (a capability trade nobody has mapped), so image-mode users may be silently better served by the older model.
core_hypothesis: Multi-objective training (video plus image) with shared capacity creates measurable regressions on static-image subfamilies where video supervision is misaligned with fine spatial detail, e.g., because video masks are temporally smoothed and lower-detail than SA-1B annotations.

one_line_idea: SAM2 has a hard forgetting horizon set by its memory capacity: reacquisition probability after occlusion collapses at a critical occlusion duration (a cliff, not a slope), and the cliff location is a fixed architectural constant rather than content-dependent.
core_hypothesis: Because the memory bank holds a bounded number of recent frames plus prompted frames, occlusions longer than the effective temporal span evict all target evidence except the distant prompt, producing a sharp phase transition in reacquisition probability whose location depends on memory configuration, frame rate, and eviction policy, but only weakly on scene content.

one_line_idea: For video domain shift, adapting only SAM2's memory-attention layers beats adapting the image encoder at equal parameter budget: domain gap in video lives in temporal association, not appearance encoding.
core_hypothesis: Cross-domain failures in video segmentation are dominated by memory retrieval errors (wrong temporal association under new motion and appearance-change statistics) rather than frame-level encoding errors, so memory-attention LoRA recovers more tracking accuracy per parameter than encoder LoRA.

one_line_idea: SAM2's occlusion prediction is a motion-prior guess, not an evidence-based judgment: it infers disappearance from motion patterns rather than from what pixels show, failing lawfully on static occlusions and motionless disappearances.
core_hypothesis: Occlusion-head accuracy is high when occlusion co-occurs with characteristic motion signatures (as in web video training data) and collapses when occlusion is decoupled from motion (static object occluded by another static object after a camera pan, object occluded without either moving), revealing the head learned motion-occlusion correlation rather than visibility reasoning.

one_line_idea: SAM2 has a preferred temporal sampling rate: tracking accuracy is non-monotone in frame rate, peaking near training-video statistics, so both slowing down and speeding up input degrades it, contrary to the assumption that more frames never hurt.
core_hypothesis: Memory retrieval and update were optimized for the inter-frame displacement distribution of training videos, so both under-sampling (too much change per step) and over-sampling (near-duplicate frames flooding memory slots and diluting temporal diversity) reduce accuracy, producing an inverted-U response to frame rate.

one_line_idea: Propagation in SAM2 is temporally asymmetric beyond content effects: propagating a middle-frame prompt backward is systematically worse than forward, revealing an architectural arrow of time that batch (offline) video adaptation should exploit or repair.
core_hypothesis: Training predominantly on forward-streaming episodes taught memory attention forward-conditional statistics (how objects evolve forward in time), so backward propagation runs the model off its learned conditional distribution even on time-symmetric content, producing an accuracy gap that persists on reversibility-controlled clips.

one_line_idea: Adapting SAM2 on domain video corrupts its image-mode promptability faster than adapting SAM1 on matched images does, because gradients through memory attention couple the static pathway to temporal objectives, making video PEFT uniquely forgetting-prone.
core_hypothesis: In SAM2, image-mode behavior shares parameters with temporally-conditioned computation, so video-domain gradients perturb static-mode functions in ways image-domain gradients (in SAM1 adaptation) do not, yielding faster degradation of image-mode metrics per unit of target-domain gain.

one_line_idea: Model-in-the-loop data generation gave SAM a mask-style monoculture: SA-1B's semi-automatic pipeline filtered out messy, low-compactness masks, so SAM inherits a compactness prior that is a data-flywheel artifact, not a property of the visual world.
core_hypothesis: The distribution of mask complexity (boundary fractal dimension, concavity counts) in SA-1B is significantly narrower than in fully-manual datasets of comparable content, and SAM's error rate grows with a target mask's distance from the SA-1B complexity mode faster than content difficulty explains.

one_line_idea: SAM carries a photographic-composition prior: mask quality for identical content varies with its position in the frame (center and rule-of-thirds hotspots), an artifact of professional photography in SA-1B that surveillance and industrial imagery violates wholesale.
core_hypothesis: Because professional photos concentrate subjects at compositional hotspots, SAM's per-location accuracy map (same object pasted at controlled positions) is non-uniform with peaks at center and thirds intersections, and the non-uniformity shrinks in models trained on uncurated data.

one_line_idea: Class-agnostic training left latent semantics in SAM: its masks snap to semantic category boundaries even when low-level evidence contradicts them, so SAM is a covert semantic segmenter whose hidden classes bias supposedly geometry-only outputs.
core_hypothesis: Mask boundaries preferentially align with human category boundaries (person vs background, object vs shadow) even under adversarially-matched low-level contrast, because annotators segmented nameable things, injecting semantics into supposedly class-agnostic supervision.

one_line_idea: SAM has a viewpoint prior from licensed photography: performance drops lawfully with deviation from eye-level, subject-facing viewpoints, making overhead, egocentric, and oblique-angle imagery systematically underserved for reasons unrelated to content.
core_hypothesis: For matched scenes and objects, accuracy is a decreasing function of viewpoint distance from the photographic canon (elevation and tilt statistics of professional photos), and viewpoint explains a large share of the deficit currently attributed to domain gap in aerial and egocentric benchmarks.

one_line_idea: SAM's part-vs-whole ambiguity resolution is anchored to SA-1B's mask-size distribution: when object-to-image size ratios leave the training regime, granularity choices become systematically biased (macro shots yield parts, distant shots yield groups) independent of prompt intent.
core_hypothesis: The learned prior over selected-mask scale is anchored to the absolute mask-area distribution of SA-1B, so for images whose true-object area ratio is off-distribution, the top-ranked granularity shifts toward the prior mode, producing predictable part-selection at high magnification and group-selection at low magnification.

one_line_idea: Guideline archaeology: SAM's handling of pathological cases (wires, fences, reflections, transparent objects) encodes recoverable traces of SA-1B annotation-guideline decisions, showing that foundation models memorize policy, not just imagery.
core_hypothesis: For structure classes where annotation guidelines forced a convention, SAM's outputs are more consistent (lower cross-image entropy of topological choices) than for classes where guidelines were silent, revealing policy memorization distinguishable from evidence-driven behavior.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Guideline archaeology: foundation models memorize annotation policy, not just imagery. Opens a data-provenance forensics line.

one_line_idea: SA-1B's grid-prompt generation left a periodic spatial fingerprint in SAM: averaged over many images, mask-probability and mask-seed statistics show energy at the generation grid frequency, an unnoticed artifact coupling dataset construction to model prior.
core_hypothesis: Masks in SA-1B's automatic stage were seeded from regular point grids, biasing the retained-mask spatial statistics; SAM internalized this as a weak periodic prior detectable by averaging click-response maps or everything-mode seed statistics over thousands of images in grid-aligned coordinates.

judge_c.anomaly_note: SA-1B grid-prompt fingerprint inside SAM's prior: dataset-construction artifact detectable in the model. Unusual and cheap to test.

one_line_idea: Benchmark mIoU anti-correlates with interactive usability across PEFT methods: adapters that win static benchmarks require more correction clicks in deployment because they trade prompt responsiveness for prompt-independent priors.
core_hypothesis: Adaptation that maximizes single-shot accuracy does so partly by strengthening domain priors that override prompt details; such prior-heavy models respond weakly to corrective clicks, so single-shot accuracy and interactive efficiency are anti-correlated across adapted checkpoints within a domain.

judge_c.anomaly_note: mIoU anti-correlates with interactive usability across PEFT methods: directly attacks the field's selection criterion.

one_line_idea: Boundary metrics conflate constant offset with jitter: decomposing boundary error into bias and variance components changes which PEFT method wins, because methods differ in which component they fix.
core_hypothesis: PEFT methods partition into offset-fixers (whose gains vanish after optimal per-method morphological correction) and jitter-fixers (whose gains survive), and published rankings mix the two, so re-ranking after bias correction reorders a substantial fraction of comparisons.

one_line_idea: Centroid-click evaluation is a lucky-prompt protocol: model rankings among adapted SAMs invert under prompt distributions sampled from real user behavior, because centroid clicks are systematically easier than human clicks.
core_hypothesis: Model robustness to prompt-placement variation differs across adaptation methods (some narrow the prompt basin, idea 005), so the ranking of methods under centroid protocol and under human-sampled prompt distributions diverges measurably, with prompt-basin width as the mediating variable.

one_line_idea: SAM's failures are bimodal (near-perfect or catastrophic), so mean metrics track the mixture weight rather than segmentation quality, and PEFT methods should be compared by failure-rate curves instead of averages.
core_hypothesis: Per-instance IoU distributions for frozen and adapted SAM are strongly bimodal across domains, adaptation methods differ primarily in how they move mass between modes (not in shifting the good mode), and mean-based rankings therefore disagree with risk-based rankings (e.g., probability of IoU below 0.5) in a predictable fraction of comparisons.

one_line_idea: Cross-paper PEFT-for-SAM comparisons are confounded by prompt-simulation policy more than by method: a controlled re-implementation shows the prompt protocol explains more ranking variance than the adaptation technique being advertised.
core_hypothesis: Re-running representative PEFT methods under a crossed design (methods x prompt protocols) shows protocol main effects and method-protocol interactions comparable to or exceeding method main effects for common metric differences reported between consecutive papers.

one_line_idea: Corruption robustness of SAM is prompt-type dependent in a structured way (boxes resist blur, points resist occlusion, and vice versa fails), so prompt choice is a free robustness lever no pipeline currently exploits.
core_hypothesis: Prompt types inject different information (boxes give scale and extent priors robust to high-frequency loss; points rely on local features robust to geometric occlusion but fragile to blur), producing a structured corruption-by-prompt interaction matrix that is stable across datasets.

one_line_idea: PEFT concentrates adversarial vulnerability: LoRA-adapted SAM is easier to attack than either frozen SAM or fully fine-tuned SAM, because low-rank updates create a small, findable subspace whose manipulation controls the whole adapted behavior.
core_hypothesis: Adversarial examples against LoRA-adapted models succeed at lower perturbation budgets than against frozen or fully-tuned models at matched clean accuracy, and attack gradients align measurably with the LoRA subspace, establishing concentration (not just shift) of vulnerability.

one_line_idea: SAM's low-contrast failures are threshold failures, not perception failures: under fog or dim light the logit landscape preserves the object (rank order intact) but the fixed binarization threshold misplaces the boundary, so an input-conditional threshold fixes fog for free.
core_hypothesis: Global contrast reduction compresses mask logits toward the threshold without destroying their spatial ordering, so oracle-threshold masks (choosing the best cutoff per image) recover most of the clean-condition accuracy, and a lightweight contrast-conditioned threshold predictor captures most of the oracle gain.

one_line_idea: SAM's transferability to a new domain is predicted by that domain's mid-frequency spectral content: band-pass ablation shows SAM relies on a specific spatial-frequency band, and domains missing it (ultrasound speckle, low-detail thermal) fail regardless of semantic simplicity.
core_hypothesis: SAM's grouping decisions depend disproportionately on a mid-frequency band (measurable by band-stop performance ablation on natural images), and zero-shot performance across domains correlates strongly with target-domain energy in that band, better than with semantic-distance measures.

one_line_idea: SAM flips inconsistently between modal (visible-region) and amodal (completed-object) segmentation depending on prompt position relative to an occluder, an unacknowledged mode ambiguity that makes its outputs unreliable as either kind of ground truth.
core_hypothesis: The modal-amodal choice is governed lawfully by prompt geometry (distance from the occlusion boundary, prompted side) and occluder characteristics (thin occluders trigger completion, thick ones do not), reflecting mixed conventions in SA-1B annotation rather than randomness.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Modal/amodal instability governed by prompt geometry: names an unacknowledged output-semantics ambiguity with a lawful structure claim.

one_line_idea: Distillation kills ambiguity first: efficient SAM students match teacher mIoU while losing most of the teacher's hypothesis-space structure (multimask diversity, granularity control), because distillation targets the argmax mask, not the distribution over valid masks.
core_hypothesis: Standard distillation objectives (matching final masks or single embeddings) provide no gradient signal for hypothesis diversity, so student models exhibit collapsed multimask outputs and weakened prompt-granularity response even when their top-mask accuracy matches the teacher.

one_line_idea: Distilled students fail on a strict superset of teacher failures: compression does not trade failure regions but nests them, so teacher-side failure prediction transfers to students for free, enabling cheap cascade designs.
core_hypothesis: Because students are optimized to imitate teachers (not to solve the task independently), student competence is approximately teacher competence intersected with capacity constraints, predicting per-instance failure containment: cases the teacher fails, the student fails too, plus additional capacity-driven failures.

one_line_idea: Feature-space distillation preserves prompt responsiveness while output-space distillation destroys it: two certified-equivalent compression routes produce behaviorally different interactive models, and the difference is invisible to standard benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: Matching encoder features transfers the representation the decoder's prompt machinery was calibrated for, preserving click-response dynamics; matching final masks lets the student solve the imitation task with prompt-insensitive shortcuts, so interactive responsiveness (marginal effect of each additional click) degrades specifically under output-space distillation.

one_line_idea: Quantization is prompt-type biased: INT8 SAM loses point-prompt accuracy well before box-prompt accuracy, because sparse point information rides small activations that quantization noise drowns, making current quantization certifications misleading for interactive use.
core_hypothesis: Point prompts inject low-magnitude, spatially-sparse signals into the decoder whose downstream computation operates near quantization noise floors, whereas box prompts inject redundant, higher-magnitude constraints; therefore accuracy-vs-bitwidth curves diverge by prompt type, with points collapsing one to two bits earlier.

one_line_idea: Token merging and pruning for SAM encoders selectively destroys thin and small structures long before average metrics move, because merging criteria based on feature similarity preferentially eliminate the minority tokens carrying rare-structure evidence.
core_hypothesis: Feature-similarity-based token merging removes tokens belonging to spatially-small, texturally-distinct structures first (they have few similar neighbors and low total attention mass), so structure-stratified accuracy degrades ordered by structure thinness while global mIoU is flat, and a structure-aware merge criterion eliminates the bias at equal speedup.

one_line_idea: The IoU head is a free adapter router: selecting which domain LoRA to apply per image by comparing SAM's own predicted-score distributions under each adapter beats both single adapters and weight merging, with zero additional trained parameters.
core_hypothesis: Running a probe prompt set through each candidate adapter and reading the predicted-score distribution yields a competence signal sufficient for near-oracle adapter selection, because the score head (though miscalibrated absolutely, idea 023) remains relatively informative across adapters on the same image.

one_line_idea: Catastrophic remembering: narrow-domain PEFT resurrects pretraining biases that SAM's final training had suppressed (texture leakage, compact-mask preference), so adaptation can move a model backward along its own training history, not just away from it.
core_hypothesis: Behaviors suppressed late in SAM's training (errors characteristic of MAE-stage or early-data-engine-stage models) reappear under narrow-domain PEFT in proportion to how far the adaptation data distribution is from the data that drove the suppression, producing error profiles that match earlier-stage models more than a generic degradation model would predict.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Catastrophic remembering: adaptation moves a model backward along its own training history. Genuinely new framing of forgetting.

one_line_idea: Interference between simultaneously-composed LoRAs is predicted by principal angles between their update subspaces: a five-minute weight-space measurement forecasts whether two adapters can be stacked, replacing trial-and-error composition.
core_hypothesis: Destructive interference between composed LoRAs is driven by subspace overlap in specific layers (aligned directions with conflicting scalings), so a weighted principal-angle profile predicts composed-model performance drop, and orthogonality-encouraged retraining of one adapter eliminates the interference it predicts.

one_line_idea: Domain shifts share low-rank structure: one shared LoRA trained jointly on N diverse domains matches N separate LoRAs at one-Nth the parameters, implying that adaptation learns a common shift-correction operator rather than N unrelated fixes.
core_hypothesis: A large component of what each domain LoRA learns is a domain-generic correction (e.g., re-weighting frequency bands, relaxing photometric priors, adjusting decoder thresholds) so joint training finds it with minimal per-domain residual, and the shared update's singular vectors are interpretable as generic shift operators.

one_line_idea: Self-training SAM on its own confident masks converges to degenerate over-smooth segmentation because the confidence signal is style-biased (idea 023): the obvious test-time adaptation baseline is predicted to fail in a specific, diagnosable way.
core_hypothesis: Iterative self-training with score-thresholded pseudo-masks drifts the model toward producing compact, smooth masks regardless of image evidence, with measurable shrinkage of boundary complexity distribution across rounds, while true accuracy first plateaus then declines — a signature distinguishable from ordinary overfitting.

one_line_idea: Click-policy shift is a hidden domain gap: SAM was trained on simulator clicks (error-region centers), humans click salient interiors and high-contrast landmarks, and this policy mismatch accounts for a measurable slice of real-world underperformance relative to benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: SAM's interactive competence is calibrated to simulator click statistics, so evaluating with human-logged clicks on in-domain images (no image shift at all) already produces a significant performance drop, and retraining the click simulator to match human statistics closes most of that drop.

one_line_idea: Interactive correction has oscillation modes: correcting one region creates errors elsewhere with probability that grows with adaptation strength, so heavily adapted SAMs exhibit whack-a-mole dynamics that make some targets uncorrectable in finite clicks.
core_hypothesis: The correction map (current mask plus corrective click to next mask) is a learned operator whose contraction property is not guaranteed; PEFT that strengthens domain priors reduces contraction (the model keeps snapping back to its prior), increasing the rate of non-converging correction sequences measurable as limit cycles in mask space.

one_line_idea: Fine-tuning on accumulated user corrections personalizes toward the user's annotation style rather than toward accuracy: correction-trained models drift measurably toward individual annotator idiosyncrasies, conflating personalization with improvement.
core_hypothesis: Training on one annotator's corrections improves agreement with that annotator faster than agreement with a multi-annotator consensus, and a decomposition against consensus ground truth shows a substantial fraction of the learned update is style, predicting degraded performance when the model serves other users.

one_line_idea: Prompt reuse across near-duplicate images fails silently at a predictable rate: prompts transferred between adjacent video frames or repeated product shots produce degraded masks without degraded confidence, defining an unstudied reliability metric (prompt transferability) for promptable models.
core_hypothesis: Prompt validity decays with small image transformations much faster than image similarity metrics suggest (because failure sets from idea 006 move with texture, not with content), so transferred prompts hit failure regions at rates predictable from local image-gradient changes but not from global similarity, while predicted scores stay high.

one_line_idea: Resolution adaptation is a positional-encoding problem, not a feature problem: tuning only SAM's positional embeddings (all other weights frozen) recovers most of the gain that high-resolution fine-tuning provides, isolating where resolution knowledge lives.
core_hypothesis: Feature computations (attention patterns, local mixing) are largely scale-covariant, and the dominant failure at unseen resolutions comes from positional-embedding interpolation distorting spatial geometry; therefore PE-only tuning at the target resolution closes most of the gap to full high-res fine-tuning.

one_line_idea: PEFT under a fixed prompt protocol turns SAM into a prompt-ignoring semantic segmenter: adapted models' outputs become nearly invariant to prompt content, meaning many published adapted-SAM results are really measuring a learned semantic prior wearing a promptable interface.
core_hypothesis: Prompt-ablation sensitivity (output change when the prompt is moved, degraded, or randomized) collapses during protocol-rigid PEFT at a rate driven by target-dataset homogeneity, and adapted models approach the behavior of an equivalent prompt-free segmentation head trained on the same data.

one_line_idea: Loss choice shapes mask topology more than architecture choice: the focal-plus-dice convention in SAM adaptation imposes a measurable bias toward simply-connected masks, an ignored confound that may explain topology-related conclusions across the PEFT literature.
core_hypothesis: Dice-family losses, by rewarding bulk overlap, penalize topologically complex predictions asymmetrically, so models adapted with focal-dice produce fewer holes and fragments than boundary- or cross-entropy-trained counterparts at matched IoU, and reported method differences in topology-sensitive domains shrink substantially once loss is controlled.

one_line_idea: Pseudo-label bias amplification law: students trained on SAM everything-mode outputs inherit its anti-small, anti-thin biases amplified by a measurable factor, so each generation of SAM-labeled training data drifts further from reality in a predictable direction.
core_hypothesis: Bias amplification through pseudo-label training holds for segmentation: the student's size-dependent recall curve is a sharpened version of the teacher's (omission probabilities pushed toward 0 or 1), and a second generation (student labels training a new student) sharpens further, following a contraction map whose fixed point excludes small structures entirely.

one_line_idea: Binary masks are a category error for smoke: segmentation error concentrates in a penumbra band that tracks optical thickness, not annotation noise.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-pixel disagreement between any trained model and its ground truth is a monotonic function of local optical transmittance: errors concentrate where transmittance is intermediate, and this dependence persists across architectures because it is a property of the label representation, not the model.

one_line_idea: Smoke annotators implicitly choose a personal opacity threshold, so inter-annotator disagreement is predictable from local contrast alone.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inter-annotator variance at a pixel is a monotone function of how slowly opacity changes across that pixel (the local opacity gradient); annotators agree where opacity changes fast and diverge where it changes slowly, with individual annotators being self-consistent in their threshold across images.

one_line_idea: Boundary-aware losses presuppose that boundaries exist; on amorphous classes they may actively harm learning.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] There is a dissociation: adding boundary-weighted loss terms improves segmentation of crisp-boundary classes while degrading soft-boundary classes in the same dataset and training run, because the loss injects a false prior about label geometry.

one_line_idea: The extent of a fire region in an image is partly a camera property: predictions may track exposure settings more than physical fire size.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed physical fire, the segmented area produced by trained models varies systematically and substantially with exposure bracketing, and this variation exceeds the variation across genuinely different fires of similar size, making single-image fire extent an ill-posed target.

one_line_idea: Supervising with soft alpha mattes instead of binary masks changes what the encoder learns, not just what the head outputs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A backbone trained with soft alpha supervision develops internal features from which smoke optical density is linearly decodable, while a binary-supervised twin of identical architecture and data does not, demonstrating that supervision format shapes representation depth, not just the decision layer.

one_line_idea: Models inherit a blob prior from annotators and systematically erase the fractal, multi-connected fine structure of real smoke.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The boundary complexity (for example, estimated fractal dimension or perimeter-to-area scaling) of predicted smoke masks matches the annotation distribution and is significantly lower than that of physically accurate mattes of the same scenes, and this gap persists even when models have sufficient resolution to represent the fine structure.

one_line_idea: Fixing an operational opacity threshold may collapse expert disagreement about smoke extent, showing the ambiguity is definitional, not perceptual.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When annotators are given an operationalized task definition (mark the region where an object behind the smoke would be attenuated by at least a stated visible amount, with visual anchors), inter-annotator disagreement drops by a large factor relative to free-form instructions, demonstrating the ambiguity is mostly definitional and therefore removable by protocol.

one_line_idea: Inside a transparent object, foundation-model features may encode the background seen through it better than the object itself.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A linear probe on frozen foundation-model features restricted to pixels inside transparent objects decodes the background category with high accuracy but decodes glass-versus-not-glass poorly, and this asymmetry is far weaker for opaque objects, establishing background dominance in the representation.

one_line_idea: Transparent-object segmentation may run almost entirely on contour and context, collapsing disproportionately when the silhouette is occluded.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Occluding a fixed fraction of an object's silhouette degrades transparent-object segmentation much more than opaque-object segmentation matched for size and class frequency, because interior surface evidence exists for opaque objects but is near-absent for glass.

one_line_idea: Do segmentation models use refraction at all? Rendered index-of-refraction ablations can measure it directly.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model performance on rendered transparent objects is statistically indistinguishable between physically correct refraction and a counterfactual render with the index of refraction set to one (no distortion, other cues preserved), demonstrating zero use of the defining physical cue.

one_line_idea: Specular highlights may be the load-bearing shortcut for glass detection; cross-polarized imagery could collapse current models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Suppressing specular highlights (via cross-polarized capture or highlight-removal rendering) causes a catastrophic, disproportionate drop in transparent-object segmentation while leaving opaque-object segmentation nearly intact, identifying highlights as the dominant learned cue.

one_line_idea: Depth foundation models place glass at the background depth; segmentation models sharing those backbones may inherit the glass-invisible prior.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The per-image degree to which a shared backbone's depth head sees through a given glass instance predicts the segmentation head's failure on that same instance, across instances and scenes, indicating a common upstream representation choice rather than independent errors.

one_line_idea: Static single-image transparent-object segmentation may sit near an information-theoretic ceiling that humans also cannot beat without motion.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under matched static-image forced-choice conditions (patch-limited context, no motion), human accuracy at detecting glass drops toward current model accuracy, implying much of the reported gap comes from evaluation regimes that implicitly grant humans richer viewing conditions.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Human-model gap on glass may be an evaluation-regime artifact near an information ceiling; deflates an entire benchmark-progress narrative.

one_line_idea: Training on randomly sampled single raters versus the majority vote may not add noise but shift boundary placement in a consistent direction.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on per-image randomly sampled raters converge to a boundary that is systematically offset (for example toward higher-contrast image gradients) relative to models trained on consensus labels, because the loss interacts asymmetrically with rater disagreement structure rather than averaging it out.

one_line_idea: The direction of systematic over- or under-segmentation may be set by the loss function, not the data, in a predictable size-dependent way.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For each common loss (cross-entropy, soft Dice, focal, combinations), there exists a characteristic size-dependent bias curve (predicted-over-true volume ratio versus structure size) that replicates across unrelated datasets, so extent bias is loss-determined and therefore correctable analytically.

one_line_idea: Model uncertainty maps may fail to correlate with where human experts actually disagree, because they measure the wrong kind of doubt.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The spatial correlation between standard uncertainty maps (softmax entropy, ensemble variance, dropout variance) and true inter-rater variance maps is weak, because model uncertainty tracks feature-space unfamiliarity and decision-margin geometry, while rater disagreement tracks anatomical ambiguity, and these are different fields.

one_line_idea: Predicting rater-percentile contours (p10, p50, p90) as explicit nested targets, and testing when nesting is even valid.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Rater contour families are approximately nested for boundary-graded ambiguity (margins) but violently non-nested for topological ambiguity (include or exclude a satellite lesion), so quantile-mask methods are valid on a measurable subset of cases identifiable in advance.

one_line_idea: Models may learn institution-specific contouring conventions so strongly that the annotating institution is decodable from predicted masks alone.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A classifier can predict the training-label institution from the geometry of predicted masks alone (no image input) at well above chance, demonstrating that convention style, not just anatomy, is baked into predictions.

one_line_idea: Ambiguous pixels and difficult pixels are different populations, possibly anti-correlated, and current methods conflate them.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Ambiguity (rater variance) and difficulty (model error at rater-consensus pixels) occupy substantially different image regions, with modest or even negative spatial correlation, implying that methods optimizing hard pixels are spending capacity on irreducible ambiguity while missing tractable difficulty.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Ambiguity and difficulty are different, possibly anti-correlated pixel populations; most uncertainty work conflates them.

one_line_idea: Lesion-level detection ranking versus voxel-overlap ranking: the field may be selecting architectures that reliably miss small lesions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-ranking a broad set of published-style architectures by lesion-level detection F-score produces a materially different ordering than Dice ranking on the same data, and the divergence grows as lesion size shrinks, indicating that benchmark-driven selection has been optimizing against clinical priorities on small findings.

one_line_idea: Boundary voxels are physical mixtures (partial volume): regressing mixture fractions may beat classification and match physics on phantoms.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On phantoms with known sub-voxel geometry, classification-trained models place boundaries with a systematic offset determined by the point-spread function, while mixture-fraction regression recovers the true interface with near-zero bias, and the correction transfers to real scans as improved volume accuracy.

one_line_idea: Promptable segmentation foundation models may exhibit a measurable snapping field: masks jump to the nearest high-contrast contour regardless of prompt intent on amorphous targets.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed image, the mapping from click-prompt position to output mask is piecewise constant with basins bounded by photometric contours, and on amorphous regions the basins collapse onto surrounding crisp structures, so the model is structurally incapable of returning the diffuse region regardless of prompt placement.

one_line_idea: Prompt-output variance as a free ambiguity detector: the spread of masks under prompt jitter may track true target ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The variance of masks produced under small prompt perturbations correlates strongly with independent ambiguity measures (multi-rater variance in medical images, opacity gradation in smoke), making promptable models zero-shot ambiguity meters even where their point predictions are poor.

one_line_idea: Foundation-model failure on hard domains may be predictable from the mismatch between target scale statistics and pretraining object-scale priors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Zero-shot and lightly fine-tuned foundation-model performance on a target class is predictable from a scale-prior mismatch score (divergence between the class's scale-context statistics and the pretraining distribution), across medical, smoke, and transparency domains, better than domain identity predicts it.

one_line_idea: Scaling pretraining data may asymptote for transparency and smoke because the missing ingredient is label ontology, not pixels.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across checkpoints of increasing pretraining scale, performance on opaque-object segmentation grows steadily while performance on transparency and participating-media segmentation plateaus early, because the pretraining objective never demands the multi-layer photometric decomposition those classes require; the gap is ontological, not statistical.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Scaling asymptote as ontology failure, not data shortage: pretraining scale cannot buy what the label space cannot express.

one_line_idea: Text-prompted segmentation may ground count nouns better than mass nouns, disadvantaging smoke, fluid, and tissue categories linguistically.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Controlling for visual difficulty, open-vocabulary segmentation accuracy is systematically lower for mass-noun categories than count-noun categories, and the gap shrinks when mass nouns are rephrased as pseudo-count expressions (a cloud of smoke, a pool of water), demonstrating a linguistic rather than visual origin.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Mass-noun linguistic penalty in text-prompted segmentation: a language-side cause for vision-side failure. Cross-modal and cheap.

one_line_idea: A linear-separability audit of frozen foundation features across hard domains: is the deficit in the features or in the decoders?
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Linear separability of hard-domain pixels in frozen feature space is substantially lower than for matched-frequency opaque classes, and crucially, the separability gap accounts for most of the end-to-end performance gap, locating the failure in representation rather than decoding.

one_line_idea: Under ambiguity, foundation segmenters may output confident all-or-nothing masks with a detectable bimodal signature instead of graded responses.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across an ambiguity-graded stimulus continuum, foundation-model mask areas follow a bimodal distribution with a sharp transition zone, while both human responses and properly calibrated probabilistic models transition smoothly, and the transition point is unstable across seeds and augmentations.

one_line_idea: IoU on soft-boundary targets mostly measures whether the model guessed the annotator's threshold, not whether it perceived the medium.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For amorphous-class benchmarks, a large fraction of between-model IoU differences is eliminated when each model is evaluated at its per-image oracle threshold, demonstrating that the leaderboard signal is dominated by threshold agreement rather than perceptual quality.

one_line_idea: Boundary-quality metrics on fractal boundaries may rank mask-smoothing hyperparameters, not models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On amorphous-class benchmarks, applying simple morphological smoothing sweeps to a fixed model's masks moves its boundary-metric score across a range wider than the score differences among competing published-style models, proving the metric primarily measures smoothing policy in this regime.

one_line_idea: Metric forensics: the training loss may leave identifiable morphological fingerprints in predicted masks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A classifier trained on mask morphology statistics alone (no images) can identify which of several standard losses produced the masks, at high accuracy, across architectures and datasets, demonstrating that objective choice systematically shapes output geometry independent of data.

one_line_idea: Test downstream utility directly: matting-style perceptual error may predict task usefulness of smoke masks better than IoU does.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In a simulated downstream pipeline (for example, estimating plume growth rate or visibility maps from masks), soft matting-style error measures of the mask predict downstream estimate error substantially better than binary IoU does, establishing that the field's default metric is a poor utility proxy exactly where the domain is hard.

one_line_idea: Fixed-threshold evaluation penalizes calibrated soft predictions: models honest about ambiguity may score worse than overconfident ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] There exist realistic prediction pairs (one calibrated-soft, one overconfident-crisp, equal underlying information) where standard pipelines systematically score the overconfident model higher on hard domains, and this ordering reverses under proper-scoring-rule evaluation, proving benchmarks select against honesty about ambiguity.

one_line_idea: Fire segmentation may depend on sensor saturation: HDR imagery without clipped pixels could break current models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Fire segmentation performance drops disproportionately on unclipped renditions of the same scenes (HDR tone mappings preserving flame texture), and the learned models' most salient features localize on clipping boundaries rather than combustion structure, establishing saturation as a load-bearing shortcut.

one_line_idea: When intensity and shape cues conflict in medical images, models may follow intensity even where shape says otherwise; the conflict point is measurable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On cue-conflict phantoms (lesion-shaped regions with inverted or nulled contrast, and lesion-intensity regions with implausible shapes), models overwhelmingly follow intensity, and the intensity dominance measured on phantoms predicts real-world failure on atypical-presentation cases such as isointense lesions.

one_line_idea: Smoke may be predicted wherever fire context appears: pasting fire-adjacent context into clean scenes could conjure phantom smoke masks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Compositing fire-context elements into verified smoke-free scenes induces smoke predictions in regions with no smoke-like appearance, with the induced area growing with context strength, demonstrating a quantifiable context-hallucination pathway distinct from appearance confusion.

one_line_idea: Video-compression artifacts may be a learned smoke cue: recompression could move masks more than scene changes do.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Predicted smoke masks change substantially under recompression sweeps (varying codec and bitrate on identical content), with the direction of change consistent with codec-artifact reliance, and models trained on high-compression sources show the largest sensitivity.

one_line_idea: Single-frame smoke benchmarks may leak motion information through blur signatures, inflating reported single-image capability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models evaluated on deblurred or fast-shutter versions of benchmark frames lose a substantial share of their smoke segmentation performance, revealing that part of the claimed single-frame capability is hidden temporal information rather than static appearance understanding.

one_line_idea: Smoke versus steam versus fog: current models may be undifferentiated haze detectors, and a confusability audit would expose the semantic emptiness.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On a balanced cross-media test set, smoke segmenters will fire near-equally on steam, fog, and dust once scene context is neutralized, and their discrimination ability will collapse toward chance under context randomization, showing the smoke label reflects dataset co-occurrence, not media identification.

one_line_idea: Pixelwise calibration can be perfect while extent estimates are wildly miscalibrated, because dense errors are spatially correlated; extent-level calibration is the missing target.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models with near-perfect pixelwise expected calibration exhibit severe miscalibration of derived quantities (total area, structure count, extent percentile), with realized coverage of area confidence intervals far below nominal, because correlated errors violate the independence implicitly assumed when aggregating pixel probabilities.

one_line_idea: On hard domains, feature-space distance to training data may predict errors better than the model's own confidence does.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-pixel and per-region error on hard domains is predicted more accurately by feature-space distance to the training distribution than by predictive entropy or max-probability, and the advantage of the distance signal grows with domain hardness, reversing the usual ranking observed on easy in-distribution data.

one_line_idea: Deep ensembles may agree on the same wrong crisp boundary instead of spanning plausible contours, underestimating ambiguity in a systematic direction.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On multi-rater structures, ensemble member disagreement is significantly smaller than rater disagreement, and member boundaries cluster tightly around a single mode even when raters are multimodal, demonstrating that ensemble spread systematically underestimates structured ambiguity rather than estimating it noisily.

one_line_idea: Naive pixelwise conformal prediction for masks may deliver nominal marginal coverage while structure-level coverage is near zero.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pixelwise conformal segmentation on hard domains exhibits the predicted marginal-joint coverage gap at extreme magnitude (nominal per-pixel, near-zero per-structure), and the gap is worst exactly where errors are most correlated (amorphous regions), making structure-level conformal scores a necessary redesign, not a refinement.

one_line_idea: Boundary ambiguity wants soft maps; topological ambiguity wants mask sets: a dissociation experiment could establish the representation-ambiguity matching law.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Downstream decision quality (simulated planning or alarm decisions) shows a double dissociation: soft maps support boundary-graded ambiguity as well as mask sets at lower cost, but fail catastrophically on multimodal structural ambiguity (include or exclude a satellite region), where small diverse mask sets dominate; hence representation should be selected by measured ambiguity modality.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Representation-ambiguity matching law (soft maps vs mask sets, double dissociation): would organize the uncertainty-representation literature.

one_line_idea: Confidence-correctness correlation may invert on transparent objects: models could be most confident exactly where glass fools them.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Restricted to transparent-object regions, per-pixel confidence-correctness rank correlation is negative for standard models (higher confidence predicts higher error), because confident background perception is precisely the transparency failure, whereas opaque-region correlations stay positive.

one_line_idea: Calibrating segmentation to asymmetric downstream costs may require spatially varying thresholds that no global calibration can express.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Decision-theoretically optimal segmentation under realistic spatial cost maps requires thresholds varying by location and context, and the utility gap between globally thresholded and spatially cost-calibrated outputs is substantial on ambiguous structures, establishing utility calibration as a distinct problem from probability calibration.

one_line_idea: Beer-Lambert attenuation suggests log-transmittance, not alpha, as the natural regression target for smoke; conditioning of the loss landscape may differ measurably.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training identical networks to predict log-transmittance instead of alpha yields systematically better recovery of thick-smoke structure and better extrapolation across density regimes on synthetic data with known ground truth, because the target parameterization linearizes the physically multiplicative process.

one_line_idea: Thin and thick smoke are different physical regimes (single versus multiple scattering); training data may cover one and models may silently fail on the other.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model error stratified by physical scattering regime (estimable on synthetic data and approximable on real data via background visibility) shows a sharp regime asymmetry that aggregate metrics conceal, and models trained thin fail thick (and vice versa) far more than smooth interpolation would predict, because the regimes present effectively different visual tasks.

one_line_idea: Fire is an emitter, not a reflector: emissive regions violate learned shading priors, and characteristic halo errors around flames may be the fingerprint.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Segmentation errors around fires are spatially organized by the flame's illumination field: false positives concentrate on flame-lit surfaces and false negatives inside emission cores, and matched rendered scenes with emissive versus externally lit fire-shaped objects reproduce the error structure, establishing the reflectance prior as the cause.

one_line_idea: Polarization may carry the signal RGB lacks for glass and smoke: small polarization probes could beat large RGB foundation models, proving an information gap rather than a model gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On matched capture sets, a small model with polarimetric input outperforms the strongest available RGB foundation models on transparent-surface and smoke delineation, and the advantage concentrates exactly on cases RGB models fail bimodally, demonstrating the bottleneck is sensing information, not model capacity.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Information gap vs model gap: a small polarimetric probe beating RGB foundation models would redirect effort from scale to sensing.

one_line_idea: Modeling the scanner's point-spread function inside the label likelihood may correct a systematic boundary bias that no amount of data can fix.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Incorporating a known or estimated PSF into the segmentation likelihood (predicting pre-blur anatomy that, when convolved, explains the image and annotation) removes a boundary offset that standard training provably retains, with the offset magnitude scaling with PSF width, demonstrable on phantoms and transferable across devices.

one_line_idea: Smoke, fog, and haze are points in one scattering-parameter space: regressing physical parameters might generalize where classification fundamentally cannot.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Networks trained to regress continuous scattering parameters from images generalize across media categories far better than category classifiers trained on the same scenes, and category decisions derived post hoc from regressed parameters match or beat direct classification even in-domain, showing the categorical formulation was the bottleneck.

one_line_idea: Smoke casts shadows that encode its optical thickness; models likely ignore this free evidence, and shadow-occlusion counterfactuals can prove it.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Current smoke segmenters derive negligible information from cast shadows: editing shadows out of scenes (or injecting fake plume shadows) leaves plume masks statistically unchanged, whereas an ideal observer analysis on the same scenes shows shadows contain substantial disambiguating information, quantifying an unused evidence channel.

one_line_idea: Smoke is a process, not an object: tiny temporal models may beat huge single-frame foundation models at equal compute because the signal lives in dynamics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At matched inference compute, small models consuming short temporal windows outperform the largest single-frame models on faint-smoke segmentation by a wide margin, and the advantage grows as opacity decreases, establishing that for participating media the information bottleneck is temporal access, not model capacity.

one_line_idea: Combustion imposes characteristic flicker dynamics on flames; frame-trained models cannot represent them, and the deficit is measurable as a specific hard-negative failure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On a hard-negative suite of flame-like static and dynamic confusers, frame-based models exhibit high false-positive rates that temporal models reduce dramatically by exploiting flicker statistics, and the false positives that remain for temporal models are precisely confusers sharing flame-like temporal spectra (true reflections of real fire), confirming the spectral mechanism.

one_line_idea: If smoke-extent ambiguity is structured rather than noisy, temporal averaging of predictions will not shrink it at the rate independent noise predicts; the deviation measures ambiguity structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The variance of temporally aggregated extent estimates decays much slower than the reciprocal of frame count for smoke (structured ambiguity) but near-nominally for crisp moving objects (independent noise), and the decay-rate deficit quantifies the fraction of extent uncertainty that is structural and cannot be averaged away.

one_line_idea: Optical-flow-based pseudo-labeling breaks on participating media: flow tracks the background through smoke, making motion supervision anti-correlated with the medium.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In standard motion-segmentation pseudo-labeling pipelines applied to smoke scenes, the medium is assigned to the background layer at a rate far exceeding chance, and models trained on such pseudo-labels perform worse on smoke than models trained with no motion supervision at all, demonstrating actively harmful supervision.

one_line_idea: Predicting spread-rate fields instead of extent masks: the derivative of the process may be more annotator-stable and decision-relevant than its instantaneous state.
