core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inter-annotator agreement on local spread vectors (direction and rate of the advancing front over a short interval) is substantially higher than agreement on instantaneous extent for the same scenes, and models trained on spread targets achieve higher agreement with held-out consensus than extent-trained models retrofitted to spread estimation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Predict the spread-rate derivative, not the state: re-poses the task around what is annotator-stable and decision-relevant.

one_line_idea: Object-permanence priors in video models may actively harm dissipating-target tracking: memory mechanisms could hold onto smoke that no longer exists.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Memory-equipped video segmenters exhibit systematic lag in releasing dissipated media (phantom persistence time growing with memory depth), while memoryless per-frame models release immediately, and the persistence artifact transfers across scenes, establishing permanence priors as the cause rather than appearance residue.

one_line_idea: Event cameras may separate real flames from reflections of flames by capturing combustion microdynamics invisible at standard frame rates.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Event-stream statistics over flame regions occupy a signature regime distinct from reflected or displayed fire in ways learnable by small classifiers with high accuracy, while frame-based inputs at standard rates cannot separate the pair, demonstrating a modality-specific solution to a modality-created problem.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Event-camera combustion microdynamics separating real flames from depictions: hardware-level contrarian, crisp signature claim.

one_line_idea: Longitudinal context may collapse margin ambiguity in medical segmentation: growth direction could disambiguate boundaries that single scans cannot.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Providing raters with registered prior scans reduces inter-rater margin disagreement substantially on infiltrative lesions, and models consuming registered longitudinal pairs reproduce this ambiguity reduction, showing that part of what the field calls aleatoric ambiguity is actually missing-context epistemic uncertainty.

one_line_idea: A fixed two-layer decomposition (medium plus background) may resolve most single-label errors in scenes with participating media, measuring the representational ceiling of flat segmentation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-decoding the same frozen features into a two-layer output (medium opacity layer plus background semantics layer) reclassifies a majority of smoke-scene errors as correct-under-representation, and the residual error better predicts downstream task failure than the original flat error did, establishing the flat label space as the dominant error source in participating-media scenes.

one_line_idea: Boundary ambiguity may be low-dimensional in signed-distance space: rater variation could compress to a few modes, enabling compact ambiguity representations.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Principal-component analysis of rater contour sets in signed-distance representation shows that a handful of modes explains most inter-rater variance for margin-type ambiguity across structures and datasets, and that per-pixel independent uncertainty models waste capacity modeling directions in which no rater variation exists.

one_line_idea: Occupancy and opacity are conflated in smoke labels: annotators answer different questions on different pixels, and decomposing the two could resolve apparent label inconsistency.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-annotating a smoke subset with separate occupancy and opacity questions reveals that a substantial fraction of apparent inter-annotator disagreement under the standard protocol is criterion disagreement (annotators answering different questions consistently), not perceptual disagreement, and models trained on the decomposed labels show better cross-dataset transfer because the target semantics are finally well-defined.

one_line_idea: Decoder upsampling architecture may impose a high-frequency prior that actively fights soft-boundary targets; frequency-response analysis of decoders could expose it.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Measuring decoder transfer characteristics (output frequency content given controlled feature perturbations) reveals systematic high-frequency amplification, and this amplification quantitatively predicts each architecture's error on soft-boundary targets while being uncorrelated with crisp-target error, isolating a component of hard-domain failure that lives entirely in the decoder design.

one_line_idea: Patch tokenization may quantize extent estimates in patch-size units on low-contrast boundaries, leaving a periodic fingerprint in error histograms.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Signed boundary-error distributions of transformer-based segmenters on low-contrast boundaries exhibit periodic structure at the patch frequency (and its harmonics), absent in convolutional models and absent on high-contrast boundaries, demonstrating tokenization-induced quantization of dense outputs exactly where evidence is weakest.

one_line_idea: Partial coverage and uncertainty are confounded in soft masks: a probability of one half can mean half-covered or fully-unknown, and the two need different downstream actions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on standard soft targets internally entangle coverage and uncertainty irrecoverably (no probe can separate constructed half-coverage from ambiguous-full-coverage stimuli), whereas a two-channel formulation (coverage estimate plus confidence) trained on data where the two factors are independently controlled disentangles them and improves downstream decisions that depend on the distinction.

one_line_idea: Query-based mask decoders presuppose countable instances; on uncountable media they may fragment continua into phantom instances with a measurable signature.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On continuous media, query-based decoders produce fragmentation whose piece boundaries are unstable under tiny input perturbations and correlate with query initialization rather than image structure, while dense-decoder baselines show stable continuous masks, identifying instance-prior fragmentation as a distinct, diagnosable failure mode of the query paradigm on this territory.

one_line_idea: Predicting the level-set family instead of one mask: supervising all thresholds of a soft target simultaneously may regularize amorphous learning better than any single-threshold label.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training with a monotonicity-constrained level-set objective (the model must produce a consistent nested family reproducing soft-target orderings) yields better cross-dataset generalization on amorphous classes than binary or unconstrained soft regression at matched capacity, because the ordering constraint encodes the physically correct structure of the target without committing to any threshold.

one_line_idea: The annotation tool is a hidden co-author of smoke datasets: brush versus polygon tooling may leave decodable signatures that models then learn as target structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The annotation tool used is decodable from mask geometry at high accuracy on amorphous classes (but only weakly on crisp classes), and models trained on single-tool datasets reproduce tool-specific geometry on new images, demonstrating measurable tool-bias inheritance concentrated exactly where image evidence is weakest.

one_line_idea: The sim-to-real gap for smoke may concentrate in the thin-smoke regime where renderers approximate scattering most aggressively, making synthetic data mis-teach exactly the hard cases.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on synthetic smoke show a sim-to-real transfer gap that is strongly opacity-dependent, largest at low opacity, and traceable to identifiable renderer approximations (scattering order, noise spectra), so improving renderer fidelity only in the thin regime recovers most of the transfer loss at a fraction of the rendering cost.

one_line_idea: Sparse physical sensor labels (particulate, thermal) may beat dense human labels per unit cost for training calibrated smoke extent models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For calibrated extent and density estimation (as opposed to benchmark IoU against human masks), models trained on sparse physical labels plus unlabeled images dominate models trained on equal-cost dense human annotation, because objective point supervision anchors the physical scale that human thresholds cannot provide.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Sparse physical sensor labels beating dense human labels per dollar: attacks the annotation-centric worldview with a costed prediction.

one_line_idea: Asking annotators for explicit dont-know bands may buy more calibration per annotation dollar than collecting more raters.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At matched annotation budget, single-rater tri-map elicitation produces training targets that yield better-calibrated models on ambiguous boundaries than multi-rater binary aggregation, because the unsure band directly encodes the quantity that multi-rater variance only estimates noisily through few samples.

one_line_idea: A measurable share of cross-site medical performance drop may be label-convention shift, isolable by re-contouring a subset under a unified protocol.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-contouring a target-site evaluation subset by source-site-convention annotators recovers a substantial fraction of the measured cross-site performance drop, proving that current transfer numbers conflate model degradation with ground-truth redefinition and overstate the image-shift problem.

one_line_idea: Active learning in ambiguous domains may spend its budget on irreducibly ambiguous pixels; separating ambiguity from epistemic uncertainty could double acquisition efficiency.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In smoke and medical segmentation, a large fraction of pixels selected by standard uncertainty acquisition falls in high-rater-disagreement regions where additional labels add noise rather than signal, and an acquisition function that discounts estimated ambiguity achieves equivalent performance with substantially less annotation, quantifying the ambiguity tax on active learning.

one_line_idea: Copy-paste augmentation is physically invalid for participating media: pasted smoke without recomputed attenuation may teach models compositing artifacts as the cue.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Smoke models trained with naive copy-paste augmentation respond more strongly to compositing artifacts than to physical smoke cues (verified by artifact-only probes), and physically corrected compositing (attenuation-aware blending) removes this artifact reliance while preserving augmentation benefits, isolating a data-pipeline cause of real-world brittleness.

one_line_idea: A boundary-evidence spectrum may organize all hard domains: failure modes may cluster by evidence type (photometric, geometric, semantic) rather than by application domain.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Error-map statistics (spatial error decompositions, failure signatures) from models across the three domains cluster by boundary-evidence type rather than by domain when analyzed blind, establishing evidence type as the true taxonomy of hard dense prediction and domain identity as a superficial variable.

one_line_idea: Ambiguity-type transfer may beat domain-appearance transfer: training on smoke might help infiltrative tumor margins more than training on crisp tumors does.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In a transfer matrix spanning domains (medical, smoke, transparency) and ambiguity types (soft boundary, geometric-only, structural multimodality), source tasks sharing the target's ambiguity type yield better fine-tuned performance on the target's ambiguous regions than same-domain sources of different ambiguity type, showing that what transfers is ambiguity-handling competence, not domain appearance.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Ambiguity-type transfer beats domain-appearance transfer: a transfer-matrix design with a genuinely surprising off-diagonal prediction.

one_line_idea: Hard-domain benchmarks may be approaching label-entropy floors: an estimable irreducibility bound could separate real headroom from noise-chasing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A label-entropy floor estimated from limited multi-rater subsamples (via disagreement extrapolation models) accurately predicts the plateau level that model performance approaches as capacity and data scale, validated on benchmarks where large rater pools exist, making remaining headroom a measurable quantity rather than a matter of faith.

one_line_idea: A shared learned contrast operator may underlie failures across glass, smoke, and lesions: adversarial contrast perturbations might transfer across all three domains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Adversarial perturbations optimized to degrade boundary detection on one hard domain transfer to the other two at rates far exceeding cross-domain transfer measured on crisp-object controls, indicating a shared contrast-processing bottleneck as the common cause of hard-domain failure.

one_line_idea: Models may fail differently from humans on hard domains in a complementary way, implying human-model teams have more headroom here than anywhere else.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-case and per-region failure correlations between humans and models are substantially lower on smoke, transparency, and infiltrative-margin tasks than on crisp segmentation tasks, and a simple arbitration rule exploiting the measured complementarity outperforms both alone by a margin unattainable on crisp tasks.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Human-model failure complementarity largest on hard domains: quantifies where teams (not models) have headroom.

one_line_idea: Partitioning benchmark error into information-absent, information-unused, and definition-absent components: a measurement protocol for what kind of hard each hard case is.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The three components are separately measurable (ideal-observer analyses and sensor upgrades bound information absence; human-with-tools performance bounds usable information; instruction-manipulation and rater studies bound definitional ambiguity), and applying the protocol to this territory's benchmarks will show the components have very different proportions across medical, smoke, and transparency, explaining why remedies transfer poorly.

one_line_idea: Distribution-matching evaluation: a large share of persistent hard-domain errors might be re-scored as acceptable answers under the rater distribution, changing what counts as progress.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under distribution-matching evaluation (a prediction is correct where it falls within the empirical rater distribution), a substantial fraction of state-of-the-art model error on ambiguous structures disappears, and model rankings change, revealing that current one-mask evaluation systematically misrepresents both absolute and relative performance in this territory.

one_line_idea: Zero-shot vision-language classifier calibration is dominated by prompt template choice rather than model quality, making calibration leaderboards prompt artifacts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across-model variance in expected calibration error is smaller than within-model variance induced by reasonable prompt template changes, so calibration rankings are unstable under prompt substitution.

one_line_idea: Fixed-bin expected calibration error systematically misranks vision foundation models compared to debiased or binning-free calibration estimators.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For modern high-accuracy vision foundation models whose confidence distributions are heavily skewed toward 1.0, fixed-bin ECE bias is large enough to change model rankings relative to debiased or kernel-based estimators.

one_line_idea: In-distribution calibration of vision foundation models carries near-zero information about their calibration under distribution shift.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across a pool of vision foundation models, the correlation between in-distribution calibration error and calibration error on shifted variants of the same task is weak or absent once accuracy is controlled for.

one_line_idea: Full fine-tuning of vision foundation models improves in-distribution accuracy while systematically destroying calibration transferability relative to linear probing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Linear probes on frozen foundation features retain better-calibrated and more shift-stable confidence than full fine-tuning of the same backbone, even when full fine-tuning wins on accuracy.

one_line_idea: Verbalized confidence from multimodal vision-language models is systematically less reliable than their own token-level log-probabilities on visual questions, contradicting the intuition that self-reports add information.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On visual question answering, verbalized confidence is a coarse social artifact that clusters at a few round values and carries less error-predictive information than the answer token log-probability of the same model.

one_line_idea: Aggregate calibration hides severe tail-class miscalibration: vision foundation models that look calibrated on average are strongly overconfident exactly on rare classes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dataset-level calibration is dominated by head classes, and per-class calibration error grows sharply with class rarity, so a single number certifies nothing about tail behavior.

one_line_idea: Post-hoc calibration methods evaluated on held-out splits of the same distribution overstate their value because the fitted correction does not transfer across datasets.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Corrections fitted on one dataset transfer poorly to other datasets and to shifted inputs, sometimes making calibration worse than the uncorrected model, so the standard protocol measures interpolation rather than calibration repair.

one_line_idea: A measurable share of apparent overconfidence in vision foundation models is actually test-label error, and models are better calibrated with respect to corrected labels.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] High-confidence disagreements between strong models and test labels are enriched for label errors, so measured overconfidence partially reflects annotation noise rather than model miscalibration.

one_line_idea: Calibration evaluation for detection and segmentation is ill-defined as currently practiced because the confidence scores are ranking scores, not probabilities of any explicit event.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the event a detection score should predict depends on matching criteria, thresholds, and duplicate suppression, published detector calibration numbers are protocol artifacts that change qualitatively under alternative but equally defensible event definitions.

one_line_idea: Ensembles of vision foundation models improve calibration mostly by uniformly shrinking confidence rather than by improving the ranking of which inputs are risky.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Decomposing ensemble calibration gains into a global confidence-shift component and an input-ranking component will show the shift component dominates, meaning a temperature-scaled single model captures most of the benefit.

one_line_idea: The epistemic-aleatoric uncertainty decomposition reported for vision models is not identifiable in practice: interventions designed to change one component move both estimates.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under controlled interventions, such as adding label noise to change aleatoric uncertainty or shrinking training data to change epistemic uncertainty, popular estimators will show strong cross-contamination, invalidating the interpretation of the components.

one_line_idea: Uncertainty-method rankings established on small networks and datasets invert at foundation scale, so the field's canonical conclusions may not transfer to the models people actually deploy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Relative performance of uncertainty methods is scale-dependent: methods that win at small scale, such as sampling-based approaches, lose to deterministic feature-based approaches once representations come from large pretrained backbones.

one_line_idea: Test-time-augmentation-based uncertainty mostly measures a model's augmentation sensitivity, not its predictive uncertainty, and the two decouple under simple interventions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Augmentation variance is governed by how the training recipe handled those augmentations, so models trained with heavy augmentation look spuriously certain, and the proxy fails to track error probability across recipes.

one_line_idea: For multimodal models, answer instability across paraphrased visual prompts predicts errors better than the model's own internal confidence signals.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Semantic disagreement of answers across paraphrases is a stronger and more shift-robust error predictor than single-prompt log-probability, because it probes representation stability rather than decoder fluency.

one_line_idea: Error-detection AUROC as the standard uncertainty metric structurally favors accurate models, so uncertainty leaderboards partly re-measure accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the composition of the error set changes with accuracy, cross-model comparisons of error-detection metrics confound uncertainty quality with accuracy, and accuracy-controlled evaluations will rerank methods and models.

one_line_idea: Conformal prediction sets on large-label-space vision tasks become so large under distribution shift that they are decision-theoretically worthless, and utility-based reporting would reveal this.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under realistic shift on thousand-class tasks, maintaining nominal coverage forces set sizes into ranges that no downstream consumer can act on, so coverage-plus-average-size reporting hides practical uselessness that a utility metric would expose.

one_line_idea: Contamination of vision benchmarks by web-scale pretraining is systematically underestimated because deduplication tools detect pixel duplicates but not semantic duplicates of the same scene.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial contamination tail consists of same-scene variants that evade standard near-duplicate thresholds yet still leak test-specific information, so published contamination rates are lower bounds with material undercounting.

one_line_idea: Zero-shot performance of vision foundation models is mostly seen-shot: accuracy stratified by similarity to pretraining data reveals the claimed generalization is concentrated where near-training content exists.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-item zero-shot accuracy is strongly increasing in pretraining-similarity, and the low-similarity stratum shows dramatically weaker performance, meaning aggregate zero-shot numbers substantially overstate generalization to genuinely novel content.

one_line_idea: Annotation error rates in flagship vision test sets exceed the score gaps separating leading foundation models, so leaderboard order among top models is not measurable with current labels.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For the current top cohort on mature benchmarks, plausible label-error configurations change pairwise orderings, meaning the benchmark no longer has the resolving power for its primary use of ranking frontier models.

one_line_idea: Val and test splits of legacy vision benchmarks are non-iid due to photographer, session, and source-page leakage, inflating scores relative to honest disjoint splits.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Same-source images straddling the train-test boundary let models exploit source-specific signatures, and re-splitting by source will measurably reduce scores and change model rankings.

one_line_idea: Synthetic corruption benchmarks poorly predict degradation on real-world image quality problems, so corruption-robustness scores are a misleading proxy for deployment robustness.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The correlation between synthetic-corruption robustness and robustness to naturally degraded captures, such as low light, motion blur from real camera shake, and compression from real pipelines, is weak across models once accuracy is controlled.

one_line_idea: Benchmark aging is real: category semantics and visual distributions drift over time, so accuracy on decade-old test sets overstates accuracy on the same nominal task today.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For temporally sensitive categories, models score systematically lower on freshly collected same-protocol test items than on the original test sets, and the gap grows with collection-time distance, making benchmark age a quantifiable error term.

one_line_idea: Adaptive overfitting to reused test sets is measurable in the foundation-model era: models released later gain more on the canonical test set than on fresh replicas, controlling for capability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] With foundation models whose development loops query public leaderboards and test sets at unprecedented intensity, the canonical-versus-replica gap now grows with release date, indicating accumulated adaptive overfitting rather than pure distribution shift.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Adaptive overfitting returning in the foundation era would reverse the celebrated replication-era conclusion; release-date-dependent gap is testable.

one_line_idea: General-purpose vision benchmarks embed demographic and geographic confounds that make aggregate scores unrepresentative and cross-model comparisons unstable across subpopulations.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model rankings computed on the over-represented strata differ from rankings on under-represented strata often enough that the aggregate leaderboard order is a materially biased estimate of who is best for whom.

one_line_idea: Any fixed-feature-space distance metric for generative image evaluation is structurally gameable, and an adversarial-sensitivity audit should accompany every reported score.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For any fixed feature extractor there exist generator modifications that improve the score while degrading human-judged quality, and modern training pipelines partially find such directions implicitly, so scores drift from human judgment as optimization pressure increases.

one_line_idea: Zero-shot retrieval recall correlates poorly with the end-task utility of embeddings inside retrieval-augmented multimodal pipelines.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Beyond a threshold, recall gains stop translating into end-task gains because errors shift to failure modes recall does not measure, such as retrieving redundant or subtly misleading neighbors, so embedding leaderboards misorder models for pipeline use.

one_line_idea: Model-based image-caption metrics are circular: they systematically favor captions stylistically similar to the judge's own training distribution, penalizing accurate but differently phrased descriptions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Learned caption metrics reward distributional similarity to web alt-text style over factual visual accuracy, so systems trained toward these metrics converge on judge-pleasing phrasing, and metric gains overstate accuracy gains.

one_line_idea: AUROC-based out-of-distribution detection rankings do not survive at deployment-relevant operating points, and FPR-at-high-TPR reorders published methods.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Method rankings by area metrics and by false-positive rate at stringent true-positive requirements disagree frequently enough that leaderboard order is uninformative for deployment, because area metrics reward performance in operationally irrelevant regions.

one_line_idea: Multi-task benchmark suite rankings are unstable under reasonable task reweighting, so suite-level leaderboards encode arbitrary editorial weight choices.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For current model pools, the leaderboard order changes under many defensible reweightings, such as equalizing task families, difficulty, or deployment relevance, so suite rank is an artifact of composition choices rather than a robust capability ordering.

one_line_idea: Repeated-sampling metrics for multimodal generation conflate output diversity with capability, crediting models for stochastic variety rather than reliability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Best-of-k rankings can be driven by sampling temperature and output diversity rather than by the probability of being correct on demand, so they misorder models for single-shot deployment and invert under reliability metrics.

one_line_idea: Uncontrolled prompt-engineering budgets act as hidden compute in zero-shot comparisons, and equalizing prompt-search effort shrinks or reverses claimed model gaps.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The prompt-search budget is a performance-relevant hidden variable of the same order as model differences, and gaps between models change materially when prompt optimization compute is explicitly equalized.

one_line_idea: Linear-probe evaluation encodes a linearity assumption about representation quality, and shallow nonlinear probes rerank vision backbones, undermining probe-based pretraining conclusions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Backbones differ in how linearly accessible their information is, not only in how much information they encode, so linear-probe rankings conflate the two and small nonlinear probes will reorder backbones by recovering nonlinearly-encoded information.

one_line_idea: Frozen-backbone comparisons are confounded by head architecture and head-training recipes, and standardizing heads changes which backbone wins.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Head-recipe variation contributes score variance comparable to backbone differences on several downstream tasks, so backbone rankings are partially head artifacts and change under standardized or budget-equalized head tuning.

one_line_idea: Random-seed variance in fine-tuning is large enough that many claimed state-of-the-art improvements at foundation scale are single-seed lottery wins.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across-seed standard deviation of downstream fine-tuning scores for large vision backbones is comparable to typical claimed improvements, so a material fraction of published gains would not replicate under seed resampling.

one_line_idea: Reported advantages of self-supervised pretraining over supervised pretraining shrink or vanish on several downstream tasks once augmentation pipelines and compute are strictly equalized.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A strictly matched comparison, equalizing augmentations, compute, and tuning budget, will show that part of the claimed self-supervised advantage on downstream transfer is recipe and budget artifact rather than objective superiority.

one_line_idea: Scaling up vision models does not improve calibration under distribution shift beyond what improved accuracy mechanically implies: a negative result about scale as an uncertainty cure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After conditioning on shifted-accuracy, model scale contributes no additional improvement to shifted calibration or selective-prediction quality, so scale buys correctness but not self-knowledge.

one_line_idea: Sophisticated data-curation pipelines for vision pretraining add little beyond simple deduplication plus basic quality filtering: a controlled negative result on curation complexity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under matched token and compute budgets, a pipeline of exact plus near-duplicate removal and rudimentary resolution and caption-length filtering captures most of the downstream benefit attributed to complex curation.

one_line_idea: Chain-of-thought prompting yields no genuine gain on visual reasoning benchmarks once answer-format effects and extra-token compute are controlled: a null result behind a popular technique.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The measured gains on visual reasoning tasks are substantially explained by answer-extraction differences, format-induced parsing success, and additional decoding compute, and vanish against matched-format matched-compute baselines.

one_line_idea: Knowledge distillation from large vision foundation models transfers little beyond what label smoothing and better targets provide: a dark-knowledge null at foundation scale.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At foundation scale, matched baselines using smoothed or re-labeled targets without any teacher logits capture most of distillation's student improvement, implying the teacher's specific output structure contributes marginally.

one_line_idea: Feature-space augmentation and mixing methods that helped small-scale training deliver no measurable benefit when fine-tuning foundation backbones: a scale-dependent null.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The regularization these methods provided is redundant with the implicit regularization of large-scale pretraining, so at fine-tuning time they add nothing or slightly hurt, and their continued use is cargo cult.

one_line_idea: Synthetic training images from generative models improve downstream benchmarks mainly when the test set shares the generator's stylistic biases, and gains evaporate on independently sourced test data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part of the reported gain arises because generator outputs and popular test sets share web-derived stylistic statistics, so synthetic data teaches test-set style rather than task content, and gains shrink on freshly captured test data.

one_line_idea: Human-level performance claims in vision rest on weak human baselines, and expert or incentive-aligned human evaluation reopens the human-machine gap on several solved tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Human accuracy measured with domain-familiar annotators, adequate time, training on the label taxonomy, and accuracy-based incentives is substantially higher than the cited baselines, reversing some claimed machine-over-human results.

one_line_idea: Models beating human accuracy on benchmarks are often just out-predicting annotator disagreement: agreement-ceiling analysis reframes superhuman claims as majority-vote overfitting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Where models exceed measured human accuracy, a substantial share of the excess comes from predicting the majority-vote artifact on ambiguous items rather than superior perception, and evaluation against full annotator label distributions removes much of the superhuman margin.

one_line_idea: Ground truth is instruction-dependent: re-annotating the same images under different but equally reasonable instructions shifts model rankings, exposing benchmark truth as one convention among several.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model rankings are not invariant to defensible instruction variants, because different models align differently with specific annotation conventions, so leaderboard order partially encodes arbitrary instruction decisions.

one_line_idea: Evaluating against annotator label distributions instead of hard labels reranks vision foundation models, revealing that some models are better at truth and others at convention.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model rankings under distribution-matching metrics, such as divergence from annotator label distributions, differ materially from hard-label accuracy rankings, and the difference identifies models that capture human perceptual uncertainty versus models that exploit aggregation conventions.

one_line_idea: Model-assisted annotation has quietly contaminated ground truth: benchmarks labeled with model-in-the-loop pipelines are biased toward the model families used, inflating those families' measured performance.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Annotator anchoring on model proposals imprints the assisting model's error patterns and category conventions into the labels, so related models score higher on such benchmarks for reasons unrelated to capability, creating a self-preference loop at the dataset level.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Model-assisted annotation self-preference loops: ground truth itself is becoming model-lineage-biased. Ecosystem-level contamination claim.

one_line_idea: Quality-control gold questions bias test sets toward the unambiguous, so benchmarks systematically exclude the hard cases and overstate deployable accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The discarded high-disagreement items are not noise but a coherent hard stratum of the task distribution, and model accuracy on that stratum is far below benchmark scores, meaning quality control mechanically inflates reported capability.

one_line_idea: Vision-language models used as judges of visual outputs exhibit self-preference and family-preference biases large enough to corrupt model comparisons that rely on them.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Multimodal judges systematically favor outputs from themselves and from models sharing their training lineage, with bias magnitude comparable to the quality differences being measured, so judge-based visual leaderboards are structurally distorted.

one_line_idea: Annotation-vendor ecosystems create test-set leakage paths that deduplication cannot see: the same worker pools and internal guideline documents touch both training-data production and benchmark creation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Convention leakage through shared annotation ecosystems aligns training labels with benchmark labels at the level of edge-case handling, giving models trained on vendor-labeled data an unearned benchmark advantage invisible to image-level contamination audits.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Annotation-vendor convention leakage invisible to dedup: a leakage channel nobody audits, with a concrete fingerprinting test.

one_line_idea: A field-wide bootstrap audit of vision benchmark deltas: a large fraction of published improvements are within test-set resampling noise once paired item-level uncertainty is computed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Applying paired item-level bootstrap to a broad sample of published improvement claims will show that a substantial fraction do not exceed resampling noise, and the non-significant fraction has grown over publication years as margins shrank.

one_line_idea: Leaderboards inflate apparent state-of-the-art through selection: the expected maximum over many noisy submissions exceeds true best performance, and the bias is quantifiable from submission statistics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The winner's-curse gap between the top reported score and the top submitter's true expected performance is large enough on active leaderboards to account for a visible share of year-over-year state-of-the-art movement.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Leaderboard winner's curse quantified from submission statistics: turns a folk suspicion into an estimable bias.

one_line_idea: The vision benchmark ecosystem has low effective dimensionality: most benchmarks rank models nearly identically, so new benchmarks add publication events but little measurement information.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The cross-model score matrix over current benchmarks is dominated by one or two principal components, implying most benchmarks are re-measurements of a general factor plus noise, and claimed capability distinctions are mostly unsupported.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Benchmark ecosystem low effective dimensionality: if one factor explains most rankings, new benchmarks add events, not information.

one_line_idea: The same checkpoint scores materially differently across popular evaluation harnesses, and harness variance is an unbudgeted error term in every cross-paper comparison.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-harness score variance for identical checkpoints on identical benchmarks is comparable to typical between-model gaps, especially for vision-language tasks where extraction and formatting differ most.

one_line_idea: Silent test-informed model selection is endemic: development practices leak test-set signal into checkpoint choice, and a leakage-audit protocol can measure the resulting inflation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Test-informed selection inflates reported scores by an amount estimable from the number of implicit test queries during development, and this inflation accounts for part of the gap between published numbers and independent reproductions.

one_line_idea: Effective-robustness analysis via linear fits on accuracy scatter plots breaks down near the accuracy ceiling, and conclusions about which interventions confer robustness flip under ceiling-aware models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The linear-trend methodology produces systematic artifacts as models approach accuracy ceilings, misattributing compression effects to robustness, and re-analysis with nonlinear or logit-transformed fits overturns some published effective-robustness conclusions.

one_line_idea: Distribution-shift benchmarks conflate multiple shift types into single scores, and factorizing shifts reveals that models robust on the benchmark are robust to only some factors deployments care about.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model robustness is factor-specific, and aggregate shift scores hide large factor-level differences between models, so two models with equal benchmark robustness can behave oppositely on any given deployment's dominant shift factor.

one_line_idea: Fixed-epsilon adversarial evaluation is incomparable across models with different preprocessing and native resolutions, making cross-model robustness tables silently inconsistent.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A fixed nominal budget corresponds to different effective perturbation strengths across preprocessing pipelines, so cross-model robustness comparisons at equal epsilon are comparing unequal attacks, and perceptually-calibrated budgets change the rankings.

one_line_idea: Corruption-robustness gains from augmentation research are substantially overfitting to the benchmark's corruption menu, and generalization to held-out corruption families is much weaker than reported averages suggest.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The community has been implicitly fitting the corruption menu, so method rankings on the standard menu poorly predict rankings on freshly designed held-out corruption families, and the field's measured robustness progress partially evaporates under menu replacement.

one_line_idea: Vision models certified robust by standard suites fail on temporal shift: robustness leaderboard leaders lose their advantage on data collected years after their training cutoffs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Ranking models by standard robustness suites poorly predicts ranking by accuracy retention on temporally newer data, because temporal drift stresses semantic and distributional changes the suites do not represent.

one_line_idea: Spurious-correlation benchmarks contain their own meta-spurious cues: models can score well on debiasing tests by exploiting artifacts of how the tests were constructed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The construction process of debiasing benchmarks introduces secondary regularities, such as selection-induced attribute distributions or editing artifacts, that models can exploit to pass without acquiring the intended invariance, so benchmark passage does not certify debiasing.

one_line_idea: Certified-robustness guarantees do not predict empirical security under realistic attacks: certification radius and practical attack success are weakly related across defended models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because certificates cover threat models that real attackers ignore, the correlation between certified radius and empirical attack success under realistic unrestricted attacks is weak across defended models, making certificates a poor ranking signal for practical security.

one_line_idea: Object-hallucination benchmarks for captioning models measure language co-occurrence priors more than visual grounding, and a blind-model control quantifies exactly how much.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large share of hallucination-benchmark variance is predictable from language priors alone, so models are being ranked substantially on prior management rather than perception, and prior-decorrelated item sets change the rankings.

one_line_idea: Visual-grounding scores of multimodal models collapse under image-swap consistency tests: models answer identically when the image is replaced, exposing text-shortcut reliance the benchmarks never check.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A significant fraction of correct answers on grounding benchmarks survive image substitution, meaning measured grounding is substantially text-driven, and consistency-adjusted scores that require answer sensitivity to the image will rerank current models.

one_line_idea: Referring-expression benchmarks are substantially solvable by object-size and position priors without reading the expression, deflating claimed spatial-language grounding.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Baselines using only object size, centrality, and detection confidence, ignoring the expression entirely, recover a large fraction of reported performance, so benchmark scores mostly reflect salience priors rather than language grounding.

one_line_idea: Reported multimodal reasoning gains on text-rich benchmarks are mostly optical-character-recognition gains in disguise, separable by transcribed-input ablations.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-model differences on text-rich visual benchmarks are dominated by recognition quality, and providing ground-truth transcriptions equalizes models far more than reasoning-difference narratives predict.

one_line_idea: Video-understanding benchmarks remain largely solvable from one or a few frames even for the newest foundation models, so temporal-understanding claims are still uncertified.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The single-frame shortcut persists in the current benchmark generation because item construction economics did not change, so current temporal-capability claims rest on benchmarks that still do not require time.

one_line_idea: Counting benchmarks are gamed by dataset count priors: models predict the modal count for an object category rather than counting, and prior-decorrelated items collapse performance.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Much of measured counting ability is category-conditional count-prior regression, and evaluation on items where true counts deviate from category modes will show performance collapsing toward prior-predictable levels.

one_line_idea: Safety evaluations of multimodal models measure refusal-style pattern matching rather than harm-relevant capability, and style-normalized re-evaluation reorders safety leaderboards.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Safety scores are dominated by superficial refusal-style alignment with graders, so models can score safely while remaining capable of harm under rephrased elicitation, and style-normalized adversarial evaluation will substantially reorder safety rankings.

one_line_idea: The assumption that higher pretraining data quality uniformly improves downstream performance is wrong: quality filtering helps some downstream tasks while measurably hurting others, and the trade-off is hidden by suite averages.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Quality filters remove data strata, such as low-quality imagery, unusual viewpoints, and degraded captures, that specific downstream tasks depend on, so per-task analysis will reveal reproducible harms from filtering that aggregate reporting conceals.

one_line_idea: English-centric class names and prompts are an ignored evaluation assumption: multilingual re-evaluation of zero-shot vision models changes rankings and reveals language-dependent capability profiles.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model rankings under non-English class vocabularies differ substantially from English rankings, and English evaluation systematically overstates the relative quality of English-dominant models for the majority-world deployment contexts where other languages define the labels.
